To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Indian faculty in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) stay in the United State because of the research opportunities and career prospects in the United States.

the Indian faculty in science/engineering who stay in the United Sates are those who came to the United States to pursue higher education and who found that their research interests and career goals are best fulfilled in this country.

the majority of Indian faculty in science/engineering who are permanent residents in the us came to the us with the intention of returning to their home country, but chose to stay in the us because of the opportunities and career prospects available in the us.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how Indian faculty members in science and engineering in the us cope with the challenges associated with living and working in a different country.
the reasons why a substantial number of highly educated Indian scientists and engineers choose to stay in developed countries.
the stay plans of immigrant scientists and their families in the United States, a topic that has received scant attention in the literature on international migration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the stay plans of the Indian faculty in science, technology and engineering in the us is a result of the combination of factors that include the availability of opportunities in the us, the lack of opportunities in India, the cultural and social distance between the two countries and the ability of the Indian faculty to cope with these distances.
the brain drain from India to the United States is reversing.
the stay plan of Indian faculty in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) fields in the us is not a result of brain drain, but is a result of the brain gain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Indian faculty in the United States are not a homogeneous group and they have different reasons for staying in the us.
, in the case of Indian faculty in the us, the decision to stay is not a result of brain drain, but a consequence of brain circulation.
the Indian scientific diaspora in the United States is an example of a reverse brain drain that is not necessarily temporary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the us is still a desirable destination for highly educated immigrants from India.
the stay plan of the immigrant faculty is not a function of the brain gain or drain but is determined by the opportunities available in the host country.
the us needs to be more proactive in attracting and retaining international faculty.
